What this means for the detector dataset

  • Every file shares one format (2400×1080, yuv420p, H.264 Main, AAC 48 kHz stereo, median — Mbit/s), so no per-file preprocessing is needed beyond decoding.
  • Frame rate swings from about — to — fps inside one file, with — freezes longer than 0.5 s. Frame indices are not a clock: sample, split and track by timestamp, and expect a tracker to see uneven time steps.
  • Players are small: the median on-pitch person box is — px tall and the ball about — px across at 1080p. Train at high input size (1280 to 1920) and keep small-object augmentation gentle.
  • The pretrained COCO model finds — on-pitch people per live frame on average, against 22 players plus officials on the pitch, and sees the ball in only —% of live frames. The ball is the class that most needs labelled data.
  • Sharpness splits the recordings into two groups: — measure a median Laplacian variance of — in live play, the rest about —. That points to a different in-game graphics or recording setting on those days; check that the val and test matches cover both groups.
  • Replays, cutscenes and menus take —% of the time. The score-panel test separates them cleanly, so keep filtering them out before sampling.

Per-recording summary

One row per match. Live-play columns use only samples where the score panel and grass are visible. Click a row to pick that match for the other tabs; click a header to sort.

Time spent at each frame rate

Share of wall-clock time by instantaneous frame rate (1 / gap to the next frame). All matches, weighted by length; the picked match is drawn as a line.

Frame rate per recording

Bar spans the 5th to 95th percentile of instantaneous fps; the tick is the mean frame rate. Colour is the split.

Frames delivered each second, picked match

Dips to zero are freezes in the recording (the game or the recorder stalled). Dashed line: 30 fps.

Bitrate each second, picked match

Mbit per second of video. Spikes follow keyframes and fast camera pans; troughs are static menus and stalls.

Freezes per recording

Total time inside gaps longer than 100 ms between frames.

Frame size by type

Mean compressed size of keyframes and of the frames between them, in KB. One keyframe every few seconds (GOP column in the overview table).

Image statistics per recording, live play

Box spans the 25th to 75th percentile of the sampled frames, whiskers the 10th to 90th, tick the median. Sharpness is the variance of the Laplacian on the centre of the full-resolution frame; luma, contrast and saturation are on a 0 to 255 scale.

Same measure by game state

Distribution over all sampled frames, as a share of each state's samples.

Colour distribution by split

Hue of saturated pixels (S > 40). The grass peak near 100° dominates; the strip under the axis shows each hue. Train, val and test overlap, so the splits are not separated by colour.

What is on screen over time

Every recording, sampled twice a second. Live play shows the score panel over grass; replays and cutscenes show grass without the panel; other is menus, lineups and celebration screens; black is a fade.

Share of time by state

Scene cuts per minute

A cut is a drop in colour-histogram correlation below 0.6 between samples 0.5 s apart: camera switches into and out of replays, menus and celebrations.

Horizontal camera pan, live play

Median optical-flow shift between samples 0.5 s apart, in full-resolution pixels. The broadcast camera follows the ball left and right; vertical movement is small.

Camera speed per recording

Median flow magnitude per 0.5 s, live play. Box 25th to 75th percentile, whiskers 10th to 90th.

Frame-to-frame change by state

Mean absolute grey-level difference between samples 0.5 s apart. Near-zero values in live play are pauses (set pieces, the game waiting), which give near-duplicate frames.

People on the pitch per frame

Pretrained YOLO11m (COCO person, confidence ≥ 0.30, feet on the grass), one live frame per second. A full view would hold 22 players and up to 3 officials; the camera shows part of the pitch.

Ball found per recording

Share of live frames with at least one COCO sports ball (confidence ≥ 0.15) on the pitch.

Person box height

Pixels at 1080p, share of each split's boxes. Most players are under 100 px.

Ball size

Square root of the box area, pixels at 1080p.

Where people appear

Box centres over the 2400×1080 screen, all matches. The top strip is the HUD.

Where the ball appears

The camera keeps the ball near the middle band of the screen.

Contact sheet, picked match

Twelve frames spread evenly across the recording.

Mean and variation image, picked match

Left: the average of every sampled frame. Right: per-pixel standard deviation (dark = never changes). The dark score panel, timer and control buttons are fixed HUD regions; mask or ignore them when training and evaluating.
